reader.requirement: At --std 85, an indexed file must set each invalid key value (Amendments 1 and 2 applied in place): 21 when the prime key changes between READ and REWRITE in sequential access, or a WRITE breaks ascending order (including EXTEND's first record); 22 for a WRITE of a duplicate prime key, or a WRITE or REWRITE of a duplicate alternate key without DUPLICATES; 23 for a random access to an absent record, or a START or random READ of an absent optional input file; 24 beyond the implementor's boundary. The witness covers a, b.1, b.2 (WRITE only) and c.1/c.2 for READ and START; it does not cover b.2 for REWRITE, EXTEND, alternate-key or other-verb 23, or d.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly: the 85 arm adds the random READ's 02 look-ahead after the 23 test; the 21/22/23 arms are not switched

reader.edition-search: grep DialectBehavior|Edition in IndexedConnector.cs: only lines 445 (READ PREVIOUS, which 1985 does not have) and 580 (02). Write, Rewrite, Delete and Start consult none.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the 2x values (p1ik at 85 and p1ik23 at 2023 agree on every 2x line)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: b.2 for REWRITE, EXTEND 21, 23 for alternate-key READ, START GREATER/NOT LESS and DELETE, and d (24) are outside g85_f16_04

probes.printed: EXT21 21 IK / EXTEQ 21 IK / RW22A 22 IK / W22A-IO 22 IK / RD23A 23 IK / ST23G 23 IK / ST23N 23 IK / DL23 23 IK / RW23 23 IK / RN22 22 IK (random access) / VW22 22 IK and VR23 23 IK (RECORD VARYING with ODO)
probes.expected: a: 21 under EXTEND (§1985:IX.4.9.4 GR14, GR17a); b.2: 22 on REWRITE of a no-DUPLICATES alternate; c.1: 23 for each random access to an absent record

probes.printed: W02 02 NIK (WITH DUPLICATES alternate); DL00 00 NIK
probes.expected: No 22 where DUPLICATES is specified (02, successful); the NOT INVALID KEY branch runs

reader.notes: Opened seeds _lastWrittenPrime with the highest existing key under EXTEND, so EXTEND's first record is held to GR14. Rewrite skips its own record (self: prime) when testing alternates, so an unchanged key is never a false 22. Item d is the store's 2^32-page capacity or a host file-size refusal (StoreStatus.Boundary to 24 in RecordWriteFailed, documented in DOC-A.1-107). It was read but not probed, under the host-safety rule.

refuter.evidence: Read GRL2.3 a-d with Amendments 1 and 2 applied (C138, C278) and §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR14. r1.cob (r1-002): a. 21 only for sequential access: sequential OUTPUT K005 then K003 21 and K004 21 (the base stays at the last successful key), sequential REWRITE with the prime key changed to an existing key gives 21 and not 22, while dynamic OUTPUT K009 then K001 and random I-O K009 then K001 give 00, and a dynamic REWRITE after READ with a different prime key rewrites the named record (00) with no 21; b.2: sequential REWRITE onto an existing no-DUPLICATES alternate 22, WRITE alternate duplicate 22, random WRITE duplicate prime 22; c.1: dynamic REWRITE absent 23. r4.cob (r4-001): 'ascending' is judged by the native sequence even with a reversed PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (§1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3). d (24): implementor boundary, read not probed (host safety); RecordWriteFailed Boundary -> '24'. cite.py: 'OK §1985:IX.1.3.4 GRL2.3 (1.3.4 I-O Status) the text is in GRL2.3'; 'OK §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR14 (4.9.4 General Rules) the text is in GR14'; 'OK §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3 (2.3.4 General Rules) the text is in GR3'.
